messages.author: cd54e625d93c7378
messages.subject: saving vectors
parts:
Hi--I'm working my way through the qclwr book (working in Windows),
and I'm stuck on p.43: The text says that to save vectors you should
use the cat function.

However, when I use the cat function with choose.file as the file
argument, it lets me select an existing file or asks me if I would
like to create a new one. If I choose to create a new text file, R
prints the filename to the console, but no file is created. If I
choose an existing file, R prints the file name to the console but the
file is not altered (neither appended if I set the argument to T or
overwritten if F).

If I manually type in the file name(a pain in the neck using Windows
and I guess you have to change all the backslashes to double
slashes?), the file is overwritten but only with the name of the
vector, not the output of the vector.

any suggestions?

Ok. Let's say I'm working with a simple vector "names", which has the
following elements:

[1] "James"    "Jonathan" "Jean-Luc"

I want to print this to a text file saved n my hard drive

Here's the script I'm using at the suggestion of the book:

>cat("names", choose.files(), sep="\n")

Supposing I select the file: 03-2-4_vector-a  in the dialogue box, R
prints:

names
C:\_qclwr\_outputfiles\03-2-4_vector-a.txt

But no change is made to the file. If I paste the file name into the
script so we see something like this:


>cat("names", file="C:\_qclwr\_outputfiles\03-2-4_vector-a.txt", sep="\n")

I get the following doomsday message:

Error in file(file, ifelse(append, "a", "w")) :
 cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning messages:
1: '\_' is an unrecognized escape in a character string
2: '\_' is an unrecognized escape in a character string
3: unrecognized escapes removed from "C:\_qclwr\_outputfiles
\0-2-4_vector-a.txt"
4: In file(file, ifelse(append, "a", "w")) :
 cannot open file 'C:_qclwr_outputfiles -2-4_vector-a.txt': Invalid
argument

I looked through the R manual, and it suggested that I should double
the backslashes. So no we've got this:

>cat("names", file="C:\\_qclwr\\_outputfiles\\03-2-4_vector-a.txt", sep="\n")

R returns just the prompt:

>

leading me to believe I've been successful. But no. The text file
contains only the vector name "names", and not the elements of the
vector.

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: saving vectors
parts:
Also, try to do run the following command without the quotation marks for the object name, like that:

cat(names, file="C:\\_qclwr\\_outputfiles\\03-2-4_vector-a.txt", sep="\n")

or

cat(names,file=choose.files(),sep="\n")


I guess that, as your vector's name is "names", if you use the quotation marks there, R will think that you want it to produce a .txt file with the string "names" in it and NOT the elements of the object "names".

Let me know if that helps.

A.

Hi,

I had a similar problem with "cat" as Mark did, and tried "write"
instead.

write(x.2, choose.files(), sep="\n") # Exercise box 3.1 (1)

It worked!

Best,
Kazuto

Kazuto Matsumura
Graduate School of Humanities and Sociology
University of Tokyo

On 2009-04-20, 7:11 am, "Stefan Th. Gries" <stgr...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi
>
> You have to write
>
> cat("names", file=choose.files(), sep=" ") # cat("names",
> choose.files(), sep=" ")
>
> Otherwise, R thinks the string resulting from choose.files() is
> another string to be printed, as in
>
> cat(1:3, 4:6, sep=" ")
>
> That is, it lets you select a file name and prints it out. If you use
> the above, R knows that the string resulting from choose.files() is
> meant to be cat's file argument.
>
> Cheers,
> STG
> --

argument is the file, as you can see when you enter
